description: An invite of version 3 (PROTOCOL 20.9, ADR 0033 4): the connect ceremony hybrid with ML-KEM-768. Both renderings start with the marker "8", which neither base32 nor version 2 reads, so every older parser refuses the invite. invite_key = HKDF-SHA256(secret, salt="", info="z-connect-invite-v3", 32). Message 1 adds ek, the inviter's fresh ML-KEM-768 key; message 2 adds ct, where (ct, K) = ML-KEM-768.Encaps(ek; m), by the acceptor. Each commitment is HMAC-SHA256(invite_key, "z-connect-commit-v3:" || eph || SHA-256(kem) || u16be(len(code)) || code || name), kem being ek for the inviter and ct for the acceptor. The channel key is HKDF-SHA256(dh || K, salt=invite_key, info="z-connect-channel-v3", 32); the digits are computed as in connect.json from dh || K, with info "z-connect-sas-v3" || lo... || hi... || SHA-256(ek || ct); the mailboxes and the rendezvous id as in mailboxes.json and connect.json under "z-connect-relay-v3:" and "z-connect-rendezvous-v3:". Each reveal adds "pqk", the account's ML-DSA-65 key, which its code commits to, and "pqseal", the device's ML-KEM-768 sealing key, whose hash a code carrying "sk" names. The frames are unpadded, and frame_lengths gives each payload as the relay carries it. version_2_of_the_same_inputs records what version 2 computes from the same secret, ephemerals and identities; a client of version 3 computes none of it. The go-ahead tag is derived from the channel key exactly as group.json shows. K, ct and the KEM keys are re-derived from kem.seed and kem.m by kyber-py.
